o: Build a graph on the n rows with an edge when the rows share ≥ k distinct values, then count connected components. With n, m ≤ 100 and values ≤ 100, converting each row to a 100-bit set (or Python set) and testing all pairs is trivially fast. Examples: with k=1 rows sharing any value merge; [[1,1],[1,1]] with k=2 shares only one distinct value → 2 components.

a.i: Deduplicate each row into a set, union every pair with intersection size ≥ k, count distinct roots.
a.t: O(n²·m) — all pairs with set intersection; trivially fast for n,m ≤ 100.

w: Alternative: BFS/DFS over an adjacency matrix instead of union-find — equivalent. Pitfall: intersection counts DISTINCT common integers (dedupe rows first). Follow-up: large n would need bitset/word-level intersection tricks.
